answer: We formulate dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to penalize fabricated identities. This capital barrier analysis proves the expected payoff of identity multiplication is strictly negative, functioning as a hard walnut shell blocking the adversarial inlet of inflated influence before it descends into the deep canyon of network capture. Thus, Nash equilibrium convergence in adversarial multi-agent environments is guaranteed, forcing rational actors to abandon Sybil generation to evade liquidation.
